name: can_rx_pretask
comment: RX pre/post helper reached from the ISR path; per-index fn-pointer dispatch via table at local 0x47f5 (CALL [0x47f5,IY]).

name: can_rx_isr
comment: MSCAN0 RX interrupt handler. Reads received ID from CANRXFG (0x160/0x161), rejects RTR/IDE; dispatch loop (count=0x1c) compares (ID<<5 & 0xfff8) against can_rx_accept_id_table (local 0x4857). On match stores index->0x109f and calls can_rx_copy_msg. Clears CANRFLG RXF (0x144<-1).

name: can_rx_copy_msg
comment: Per-message RX copy: indexed by matched msg index; reads can_rx_dlc_table (0x48cb) + can_rx_bufptr_table (0x48e8), copies CANRXFG data (0x164+) into the message RAM buffer (MOVB loop). Has a fn-pointer hook table at local 0x4922.

name: can_page_dispatch_stub
comment: Small stub forwarding to page-0xe3/0xfc routines; part of the RX copy path.

name: com_extract_bitfield
comment: COM signal bit-field extractor: takes a descriptor ptr, shifts/masks a sub-field out of a source byte. Used by the per-message signal decoders.

name: acc05_epb_decode
comment: Decodes ACC_05 (0x10D) byte7 (acc05_rxbuf+7 = 0x10dd) into the CAN signal image: bit4(0x10)=ACC_Betaetigung_EPB -> acc_epb_req_state.0 (+0x2800.1); 3-bit field(mask 0x0e) -> acc_epb_req_state.1-3 (graded status/type, NOT a force cmd); bit6(0x40) -> .4. Sets freshness 0x2805.80/0x2807.1/.2.

name: esp05_epb_decode
comment: Decodes ESP_05 (0x106) byte7 (esp05_rxbuf+7 = 0x10d5): 2-bit ESP_Anforderung_EPB -> esp_epb_req/0x27fc (0/1/2, 3=nicht-verfuegbar -> error clears 0x2804.0); Autohold/Konsistenz bits -> esp_flags(0x283e), validity -> esp_flags_valid(0x283f). Preceded (0x20fc7) by 10-bit ESP pressure decode: (raw-100)*3 -> esp_pressure(0x283b), 0x3ff=invalid.

name: pwm_init
comment: PWM peripheral init: PWME(0x300)/POL(0x301)/CLK(0x302)/PRCLK(0x303), prescaler PWMSCLA(0x308), period PWMPER0(0x314).

name: pwm_output_set
comment: Low-level actuator PWM output setter (channel arg B, <3). Loads duty from per-channel config table (local 0x13e3[idx]) -> PWMDTY0 (0x31c); resets PWMCNT0 (0x30c); enables/disables PWME ch0 (0x300.0) per direction bit from 0x13e2[idx]. Preset/controlled duty -> motor drive (force regulated by current, not duty).

name: actuator_output_driver
comment: Iterates the 3 output channels (0..2): per-channel state 0x13e2[ch] + config 0x4c20+, per-channel fault checks (open-load/short/over-current), then calls pwm_output_set + enable helper.

name: actuator_channel_diag
comment: Per-output-channel diagnostic/fault evaluator (config tables local 0x4c20/0x4c22/0x4c24/0x4c25); sets/clears per-channel fault bits in 0x13e2.

name: motor_apply_task
comment: Scheduled cyclic task driving the actuator output layer (-> actuator_output_driver). No direct CALL/JSR caller -> invoked via the scheduler function-pointer table (indirect dispatch).

name: clock_pll_init
comment: CRG/PLL init: SYNR(0x34)/REFDV(0x35), waits CRGFLG LOCK (0x37.8), enables PLL (0x39.80).

name: uds_readmem_by_desc
comment: UDS ReadMemoryByAddress/DID service: sets up a {src-addr,len} descriptor (0x1075<-addr,0x1073<-len), serves the transfer, scales via EMUL(#0x100); emits UDS NRCs 0x37/0x24/0x12/0x35 on error.

name: can_rx_accept_id_table
comment: CAN RX acceptance-ID table (fixed-low page 0xFD, local 0x4857). 28 x u16, each = (11-bit ID<<5) in RXIDR0:IDR1 form; masked ANDY #0xfff8 before compare. 27 subscribed msgs incl ACC_05(0x10D) ESP_05(0x106) ESP_01(0x100) Getriebe_03(0x102) Motor_03(0x105) Klemmen(0x3C0). See analysis/can_rx_matrix.csv.

name: can_rx_dlc_table
comment: Per-message DLC table (local 0x48cb), 1 byte/msg, parallel to can_rx_accept_id_table.

name: can_rx_bufptr_table
comment: Per-message dest RAM-buffer pointer table (local 0x48e8), u16/msg; where can_rx_copy_msg deposits each payload (buffers 0x10a0..0x115e).

name: CAN0_CANRFLG
comment: MSCAN0 receive flag register (RXF bit0).

name: CAN0_CANRXFG
comment: MSCAN0 receive foreground buffer (RXIDR0:1 = received ID; +0x164 = data bytes).

name: CAN0_CANTXFG
comment: MSCAN0 transmit foreground buffer.

name: PWM_PWME
comment: PWM enable register (bit0 = motor channel 0).

name: PWM_PWMPER0
comment: PWM channel 0 period.

name: PWM_PWMDTY0
comment: PWM channel 0 duty (motor drive level).

name: can_rx_buffers
comment: Base of the per-message CAN RX RAM buffers (0x10a0..0x115e).

name: esp05_rxbuf
comment: ESP_05 (0x106) received payload buffer (8 bytes).

name: acc05_rxbuf
comment: ACC_05 (0x10D) received payload buffer (8 bytes).

name: can_sig_image
comment: Base of the decoded CAN RX signal image (RTE/COM style; consumers read via base pointer).

name: acc_epb_req_state
comment: ACC EPB request state: .0=ACC_Betaetigung_EPB, .1-3=graded 3-bit field, .4=aux.

name: esp_pressure
comment: Decoded ESP_05 brake pressure/decel (10-bit, (raw-100)*3).

name: esp_epb_req
comment: ESP_Anforderung_EPB (2-bit: 0/1/2, 3=nicht-verfuegbar).

name: esp_flags
comment: ESP_05 Autohold/Konsistenz boolean flags.

name: esp_flags_valid
comment: ESP_05 flag validity/freshness bits.

name: rte_timer_service
comment: Generic per-instance timer/counter service (INCW struct+0x11 capped at 0xc8=200); called ~115x with a handle arg (LDD #id then CALL 0x88c9,0xe6) - a debounce/timeout primitive, NOT actuator-specific (earlier over-labelled actuator_state_proc).

name: epb01_tx_descriptor
comment: EPB_01 (0x104) transmit descriptor in the fixed-low TX message table: value 0x2080 = (0x104<<5) in TXIDR form. EPB_01 carries EPB_Status(0=open,1=closed,2=moving,3=fault), EPB_Spannkraft(clamp force kN), EPB_Schalterposition(driver switch).

name: epb_actuator_set_channel
comment: Actuator per-channel command setter: sets DIRECTION (0x13e2[ch] bit1 = apply vs release) and DUTY (0x13e3[ch] from arg). Called (computed) by the apply logic to command a motor channel.

name: epb_actuator_ch_enable
comment: Sets channel ENABLE bit (0x13e2[ch] bit0). Motor channel on.

name: epb_actuator_ch_disable
comment: Clears channel ENABLE bit (0x13e2[ch] bit0). Called by the per-channel fault handler.

name: epb_actuator_ch_enable_b
comment: Sets channel ENABLE bit (0x13e2[ch] bit0); alt entry called by 3 apply-logic sites (0x78972d,0x7e88c1,0x7eec4c).

name: epb_actuator_ch_fault
comment: Per-output-channel fault evaluator (open-load/short/over-current from config 0x4c20+); disables the channel on fault.

name: rte_copy_sig_image
comment: RTE bulk getter: copies 0x44 words of the decoded CAN signal image (from acc_epb_req_state 0x2806) into a caller snapshot struct. The arbitration reads the snapshot, not the live image.

name: com_rx_indication
comment: Generic AUTOSAR-COM RX-indication handler dispatched per message from can_rx_copy_msg via the hook table 0x4922 (every real msg incl ACC_05 idx20 / ESP_05 idx21 points here). Takes the message descriptor; runs the deadline/alive update + E2E/DLC check (DLC vs can_rx_dlc_table), indexes per-msg config (handle tbl 0x5250, state 0x272c, threshold tbl 0x5277). Signal unpack (acc05_epb_decode etc.) is a separate periodic COM task reached via runtime-computed pointers.

name: com_deadline_check
comment: Per-message COM deadline/timeout state machine: loops the msg-state array (0x272c flags, counter 0x2731 +10 cap 0xfff5) vs per-msg threshold (0x5277); sets stale flag (0x272d.0) on timeout, resets on receive; handles a consistency branch. Gates whether a received signal is 'alive'.

name: rte_input_snapshot_task
comment: Cyclic task: enters a critical section, snapshots the CAN signal image (rte_copy_sig_image -> buffer 0x1251 = copy of 0x2806, i.e. the ACC EPB request+status), copies other signal groups (0x123a-0x123c), then runs the processing supervisor (JSR 0x7890a6).

name: rte_get_acc_betaetigung_epb
comment: RTE read accessor: returns ACC_Betaetigung_EPB = snapshot 0x1251 bit0 (the ACC EPB-close request). Invoked by the arbitration SWC through an RTE function-pointer port (no static caller).

name: rte_get_acc_epb_field
comment: RTE read accessor: returns the ACC_05 3-bit status/mode field = snapshot 0x1251 bits1-3 (>>1). Qualifies the ACC EPB request.

name: rte_get_acc_freshness
comment: RTE read accessor: returns snapshot 0x1252 bit0 = ACC_05 freshness/validity (set by acc05_epb_decode as 0x2807).

name: com_rx_unused_trap
comment: SWI-trap stub (block of SWI opcodes) that the RX-indication hook table points to for the len-0 placeholder message slots (idx0/1, ids 0x752/0x700) -- traps if an unused slot is ever dispatched.

name: com_rx_indication_table
comment: Per-message RX-indication callback table (fixed-low, local 0x4922; {addr16 windowed,page8,pad8}). idx follows can_rx_accept_id_table; real msgs -> com_rx_indication(0x7e4a9e), placeholders -> com_rx_special_handler(0x78b796).

name: com_rx_deadline_thresholds
comment: Per-message RX deadline/timeout thresholds (fixed-low, local 0x5277), indexed by msg; used by com_deadline_check.

name: com_msg_handle_table
comment: Per-message COM handle/config index table (fixed-low, local 0x5250), indexed by message.

name: com_unpack_3
comment: CAN signal-unpack routine (page 0xf9) dispatched from the COM bytecode config table (opcode 0xc2 03 00 len addr). One of 6 per-message unpack callbacks alongside acc05_epb_decode/esp05_epb_decode.

name: com_unpack_4
comment: CAN signal-unpack routine (page 0xf9), COM bytecode-dispatched (0xc2). See com_unpack_bytecode_table.

name: com_unpack_5
comment: CAN signal-unpack routine (page 0xf9), COM bytecode-dispatched (0xc2).

name: com_unpack_6
comment: CAN signal-unpack routine (page 0xf9), COM bytecode-dispatched (0xc2).

name: com_unpack_bytecode_table
comment: COM signal-unpack config as a BYTECODE stream (fixed-low, ~local 0x5340). Opcode 0xc2 03 00 <len> <addr16> = 'call unpack routine at addr, page 0xf9'. This is how acc05_epb_decode(0x7e4c15)/esp05_epb_decode(0x7e4f7f) + 4 others are reached -- the runtime dispatch that had NO static pointer. Resolved statically by parsing 0xc2 records; also runnable via ghidra_scripts/EmulS12X.java.

name: rte_sched_run_runnable
comment: Cooperative RTE/OS scheduler tick, arg=runnable id (<0xdc). Looks up a descriptor in the flash table at 0x7f4800+0x2390 (GPAGE-global) and per-runnable state in RAM CB array 0x1fbf/0x1fc0 (stride 4); runs the runnable when its period elapses and latches its boolean result at 0x1fc0+id*4 bit0. This is the 'SWC function mapping' — static, in-image (overturns the old RTE-runtime-dispatch-wall claim). Full enumerated table: analysis/swc_dispatch_table.csv.

name: epb_arb_apply_ch0
comment: EPB apply/release control runnable, channel 0. Schedules a decision sub-runnable via rte_sched_run_runnable(ctx->0x10+0xc), reads its result at swc CB array 0x1fc0+id*4 bit0, then calls epb_cmd_set_applybits (7ecc02) with the command. Low-speed gate: rte_read_vehicle_speed (79058c) < 0x4b1; clamp-force ramp field ctx->0x31 bits 0x7c, +4/cycle (= empirical Spannkraft 2->17 ramp).

name: epb_arb_apply_ch1
comment: EPB apply/release control runnable, channel 1 (twin of epb_arb_apply_ch0 7ed041; selects 790000 vs ch0's 79000a).

name: epb_arb_apply_combined
comment: Combined EPB apply/release arbiter runnable (reads both channel IRVs 790000+79000a). The ENTIRE speed-check + sub-runnable schedule + epb_cmd_set_applybits(7ecc02) path runs only if coding bit coding_ext_clamp_enable (0xfe074 / alias 0x2074) bit0 is set (@0x7ed681). => master gate for external clamp.

name: epb_arb_apply_alt
comment: Second EPB apply arbiter; aborts its apply branch when coding_ext_clamp_enable (0xfe074) bit0 is clear (@0x7ed8c2). Calls epb_cmd_set_applybits (7ecc02).

name: epb_cmd_set_applybits
comment: EPB apply-request SETTER. arg(ctx, cmd): cmd=100('d')=apply, cmd=0=release. Sets/clears command register epb_apply_cmd_reg (0x240): channel 0 -> bit4, channel 1 -> bit5 (selected by ctx->0x10). This is the arbitration OUTPUT. Called by the page-fb arbiter cluster (7ed041/7ed292/7ed657/7ed7b8/7edec3/7ee001/7ee054/7ee085/7ee2e2).

name: epb_apply_runnable
comment: Scheduled apply runnable (dispatch-table entry @0x7f561b). Reads enable-flag getter 78cd37; if set reads apply-value getter 78cd33, then calls epb_apply_cmd_write (7e81f6) with B=2 (close/apply).

name: epb_apply_runnable_alt
comment: Second apply runnable (sibling of epb_apply_runnable 7e88c1); reads the apply-value getters and drives epb_apply_cmd_write (7e81f6).

name: epb_apply_cmd_write
comment: Apply-command write, called by the apply runnables (78972d/7e88c1/7eec4c) with B=command: 2=close/apply, 1=open/release. Feeds the channel actuation layer (actuator_output_driver/pwm).

name: epb01_tx_status_pack
comment: EPB_01 (0x104) TX status packer. Reads command register epb_apply_cmd_reg 0x240/0x241 (BRSET) and ~30 signal getters, bit-packs EPB_Status/Spannkraft/etc into TX staging 0x17d-0x18c. NOT the arbitration (reads the command, reports it).

name: epb_status_measure_enc
comment: Status/measurement encoder runnable; reads epb_apply_cmd_reg 0x240/0x241 bits, encodes a packed status/state (buffer 0xef3/0xef4) via a small state machine (0xef8). Monitoring, not actuation.

name: epb_force_current_filter
comment: Periodic force/current measurement filter runnable (20-tick window via 0xfe9a5); reads epb_apply_cmd_reg 0x241 bit1, scales (7f6fc0) and range-checks [0xc,0xf5] into a 4-deep ring buffer 0x299f. Monitoring, not actuation.

name: rte_get_esp_anforderung_epb
comment: RTE getter: maps decoded ESP_Anforderung_EPB (snapshot 0x1288) to the internal command code -> 2(close)=>6, 1(open)=>5, else=>3(none). Port-invoked (no static caller). 6 is the SAME internal close code the ACC path (epb_map_acc_req_to_cmd) emits -> both requests funnel to one apply path.

name: epb_map_acc_req_to_cmd
comment: ACC request -> internal command mapper. Reads ACC_Betaetigung_EPB (via 78cead); ==1 => returns cmd 6 (close), else 0x23 (idle). Port-invoked. Feeds the same arbiter/apply path as the ESP request.

name: rte_get_esp_epb_consistency
comment: ESP_05 EPB-consistency/validity qualifier. Returns 1 iff snapshot[0x128a].0 (esp_flags_valid.0) && snapshot[0x1289].5 (esp_flags.5) && snapshot[0x128a].7 (esp_flags_valid.7). This is the EPB's own COM-validity gate on the received ESP_05 (NOT a second-copy cross-check).

name: rte_get_esp_autohold
comment: RTE getter: ESP_Autohold_aktiv = snapshot 0x1289 bit0. First-class arbitration input (has a dedicated getter), fed to the same decision runnable as the ESP/ACC request.

name: rte_get_esp_pressure
comment: RTE getter (LDD): ESP brake-pressure snapshot at 0x1286.

name: epb_ext_clamp_available
comment: External-clamp 'available' helper. Returns available IFF coding_ext_clamp_enable (0xfe074).0 && coding_ext_clamp_enable2 (0xfe07c).0 — the two coding bits that enable the external clamp/dynamic-brake interface.

name: epb_tx_status_pack_a
comment: EPB status/measurement TX composer: reads every signal getter (via page-e3 accessors) and stages each into a TX buffer via page-e5 writers (0x402fXX). NOT arbitration (reads-and-reports, like epb01_tx_status_pack).

name: epb_tx_status_pack_b
comment: Second status/measurement TX composer (sibling of epb_tx_status_pack_a 789c13); stages via page-fc writers 0x4036XX.

name: uds_service_dispatch
comment: UDS/KWP diagnostic service dispatcher: length-check -> sub-function/routine table (local 0x5a0b stride 9, handler ptr block 0x5a11) -> session/security/condition guards -> NRC returns 0x13(len)/0x31(range)/0x33(secAccess)/0x22(conds)/0x78(pending). Not on the control path.

name: rte_read_vehicle_speed
comment: RTE IRV read returning a vehicle-speed value; the EPB apply arbiters gate the clamp on this being below ~0x4b1/2000 (low-speed/standstill only).

name: nvm_block_read_sm
comment: NvM/EEPROM block read+verify state machine (status nibbles at 0x11dd: 0/0x10/0x20/0x30; block ctrl 0x1d4-0x1f0; compare 0x1e9 vs 0x1e7 + retry counter). Part of the boot NvM path that materializes the coding mirror (0xfe070 block) from EEPROM.

name: epb_apply_cmd_reg
comment: EPB arbitrated apply-request command register (byte). bit4 = channel-0 apply, bit5 = channel-1 apply. Written by epb_cmd_set_applybits (7ecc02) = the arbitration output; read by the status/TX reporters epb01_tx_status_pack (7eec4c), epb_status_measure_enc (799eaa), epb_force_current_filter (7ec0ab).

name: coding_ext_clamp_enable
comment: Coding/variant mirror byte, bit0 = MASTER external-clamp / dynamic-brake enable. Gates BOTH the ESP_05 and ACC_05 clamp routes (they share one arbiter). Read by epb_arb_apply_combined (7ed657 @0x7ed681), epb_arb_apply_alt (7ed7b8 @0x7ed8c2), epb_ext_clamp_available (78c87f). Alias of RAM operand 0x2074. Loaded at boot from dealer-coded NvM/EEPROM (NOT in the flash image) -> live value needs a UDS 0x22 coding read. If clear, no external clamp is possible regardless of message. Fed from the compact dealer coding/variant block (coding_variant_block 0xfdf4a) through the boot coding-explode path; the exact long-coding byte/bit that drives this flag sits behind the boot-materialized coding dispatch (not statically decodable) -> determine on bench via a UDS 0x22 coding read + variant diff.

name: coding_ext_clamp_enable2
comment: Coding/variant mirror byte, bit0 = 2nd enable AND'd into epb_ext_clamp_available (78c87f) alongside coding_ext_clamp_enable (0xfe074). Alias of RAM operand 0x207c. EEPROM-sourced; live value needs a UDS coding read. Same coding/variant flag array as 0xfe074 (see coding_variant_block 0xfdf4a); exact coding byte is a bench item.

name: swc_runnable_cb_array
comment: Per-runnable control-block array used by rte_sched_run_runnable (7e236a), stride 4: ready/enable/period bits + the runnable's boolean result at +id*4 bit0.

name: coding_ext_clamp_feature3
comment: Third external-clamp-related dealer-coding flag (RAM 0x2078 bit0), read by epb_ext_clamp_feature3_gate (FUN_7e3809 @0x7e3818) which also requires mode byte 0x25f2==0xf and helper 0x7ec9cb. Same coding/variant flag array as coding_ext_clamp_enable (0xfe074).

name: coding_variant_block
comment: Compact dealer coding/variant byte block (RAM ~0x1f4a-0x1f8x), restored from EEPROM NvM at boot (no in-image writer). Read by coding_variant_interpreter (79ad05), which tests bytes (0x1f4a/4b/53/55-5f/71-83) against VW variant constants (0x5a/0x33/0x3c/0x64/0xaa) and derives parameter/feature values. The external-clamp enable flags (0xfe074/7c/78) are dealer-coding-gated via this block; the precise coding bit -> flag map is in the boot-dispatched interpreter + the coding_flag_addr_table (0x7f4840), not cleanly static.

name: coding_variant_interpreter
comment: Dealer coding/variant interpreter (boot/port-invoked). Reads the compact variant block coding_variant_block (0x1f4a-0x1f8x), compares bytes against VW variant constants (0x5a/0x33/0x3c/0x64/0xaa), and builds a derived parameter/feature struct; commits feature flags into the RAM coding-flag array via pointer writes (immediate ptr-loads #0x2057/#0x2067/#0x2079 seen). Part of the coding-explode path feeding the ext-clamp enables.

name: epb_ext_clamp_feature3_gate
comment: Gate for a third external-clamp-related feature. Requires mode byte 0x25f2==0xf AND helper 0x7ec9cb AND coding flag coding_ext_clamp_feature3 (0x2078 bit0, @0x7e3818); returns enable in B.

name: coding_flag_addr_table
comment: Data table (~0x7f4840-0x7f4890) of coding-flag RAM addresses (0x2000-0x20ff: incl 0x2078, 0x20a4, 0x20be, 0x20d6 and the descending run 0x20c0/a0/60/40/20/00) interleaved with bitmask bytes (01/02/04/08/10/20/40/80). Candidate coding-bit -> RAM-flag map consumed by the boot-dispatched coding interpreter; exact record format NOT decoded, no clean code xref (computed access).
